clue.text: Shifty last retailer picked up tableware item

indicators.note: shifty suggests something moving about, so the letters of last are rearranged
picked up means heard, so the word for retailer is given by its sound

parts.note: a retailer is a seller

explanation.surface: A shady shopkeeper overheard talking about a dinner-table piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shifty' rearranges LAST into SALT; 'picked up' turns SELLER into its sound-alike CELLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dish or shaker that holds salt at the dinner table is a classic tableware item.

clue.text: Weep, hugging Liberal — a slovenly type

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping around, so the word for weep surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: to weep is to sob

explanation.surface: Someone cries while embracing a Liberal politician, who turns out to be scruffy.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an untidy, lazy person is called a slob.

clue.text: Former king with a line on the side

parts.note: late can mean former, as in the late chairman
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A one-time monarch accompanied by a line of something at the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral describes what is at or to the side, from the Latin for side.

clue.text: Speakers supporting company dance set up as partners in crime

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the ones it holds up
set up in a down clue means turned upward, so the word for dance is read backwards

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
orators are speakers

explanation.surface: Public speakers backing a firm's dance event, as though they were accomplices.
explanation.definitionFit: Collaborators in the bad sense are those who work together on wrongdoing, so accomplices in crime.

clue.text: Extend stage to include end of apron afterwards

indicators.note: to include means the word for stage wraps around the picked letter

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of apron

parts.note: then means afterwards

explanation.surface: A theatre stage is enlarged to take in the apron, the bit in front of the curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to extend something is to make it longer.

clue.text: Friend from Spain making a motorway turn

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A Spanish friend making a turn onto a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for a pal, borrowed into English.

clue.text: Pity, for the most part, is pretence

indicators.note: for the most part means nearly all, so the last letter of the word for pity is dropped

parts.note: shame means pity, as in what a shame

explanation.surface: A sad remark that pity is mostly just put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' trims the final E from SHAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a sham is a fake or a false show.

clue.text: Entertainer who was bound to show unconfined relief

definitions.text: Entertainer who was bound to show unconfined relief

parts.words: Entertainer who was bound to show unconfined relief
parts.note: the famous escapologist was tied up for every act, and the show ended with him free of his chains, to the relief of the crowd

explanation.surface: A performer who had to display open relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to' reads as 'certain to' but means literally tied up; 'unconfined relief' is both open joy and his escape.
explanation.definitionFit: The great escapologist Harry, whose act was getting out of chains and locked boxes.

clue.text: Mass with moral sets off destructive situations

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Mass with a moral message sets off havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets' looks like part of the verb 'sets off' but belongs to the fodder; 'off' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, whirlpools are turbulent, chaotic and destructive states of affairs.

clue.text: Flier confined by ambassador to land

indicators.note: confined by means held inside the following words

explanation.surface: A pilot kept by a diplomat until permitted to touch down.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European bunting, a bird and so something that flies.

clue.text: Adopt mainly dull and nice changes

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered in order
mainly means most of the word dull, its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: Taking on a mostly boring yet pleasant set of alterations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' cuts DULL to DUL; with NICE, 'changes' rearranges DULNICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt something into a group or plan is to take it in, a near synonym.

clue.text: Put on new clothes with fashionable source and did a turn?

parts.note: to put on fresh clothes is to get changed

indicators.note: fashionable read as able to be fashioned means the letters can be reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone dressed afresh, with a trendy source, and maybe did a twirl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' looks like 'trendy' but signals reshaping SOURCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Altering direction, like a ship or a policy, is doing a turn; the question mark flags the loose phrasing.

clue.text: Traditionalists sign after performance by soldiers

indicators.note: by means next to, so the soldiers sit alongside the performance
after puts the star sign behind what comes before it

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
action is performance, as in the actors' action
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A star sign is reported after the troops' operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Reactionaries oppose change and want old ways kept, so they are conservative traditionalists.

clue.text: Set up as prisoner and judged

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
figured means reckoned or judged

explanation.surface: Framed as a convict and then condemned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' suggests being framed, but it means arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to configure a system is to arrange or set it up.

clue.text: Observer in privy meeting with broker, half cut

parts.note: on can mean in, as in on the team
a privy is a toilet, a loo in British slang

indicators.note: half cut means the first half of broker is chopped away, leaving its back three letters

explanation.surface: A spectator in a lavatory meeting a stockbroker who is somewhat drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' is British slang for tipsy, but here it removes BRO from BROKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an onlooker is a bystander who watches events.

clue.text: Remain absorbed by tatty rug that's not as attractive

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken inside the letters that follow
tatty means worn and messy, so the letters of rug are disordered

parts.note: to lie is to remain, as in lie idle

explanation.surface: A shabby rug soaks up a stain, making it look worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tatty' shuffles the rug into UGR; 'Remain' reads as a verb about staying put, but supplies the inserted word.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of ugly means less attractive, an exact equivalent.

clue.text: Located audit set for revision

indicators.note: for revision means the letters are revised, put in a new order

explanation.surface: An accounts check was found and scheduled for redoing.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something located somewhere is sited there.

clue.text: Shape a student in accordance with convention

parts.note: a form is a shape
L is a learner driver, a student, from the L plates on cars

explanation.surface: Moulding a student so they behave by the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal means following established rules and etiquette rather than casual ways.

clue.text: Softens, finding the French trapped in leases

indicators.note: trapped in means held inside the following word

parts.note: to lease is to rent, so leases are rents
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone eases up on discovering French terms buried in rental contracts.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften one's stance, become less strict.

clue.text: Independent female protected by friendly source of power

indicators.note: protected by means sheltered inside the next word

parts.note: warm means friendly

explanation.surface: A self-reliant woman sheltered by a kindly energy supplier.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of wind turbines producing electricity is a supply of power.

clue.text: Draught beer's top for this idiot

parts.note: a draught is a current of air
the head is the froth on top of a beer

explanation.surface: A draught beer's foam goes to this fool's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draught beer' reads as one pub phrase, but 'Draught' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: an empty-headed, foolish person.

clue.text: Head of government permits spirits, showing such wit

indicators.note: head of means the first letter

parts.note: allows means permits
humour can mean mood or spirits, as in good humour

explanation.surface: A prime minister lets spirits flow, showing a dark sense of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such' points back to the clue itself: grim jokes about a government head.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim joking in the face of death or disaster is the kind of wit named after the hangman's scaffold.

clue.text: One cuts copies up in colour

indicators.note: cuts means the numeral goes into the reversed word, splitting it
up in a down clue means read upward, backwards

parts.note: to ape is to copy, so copies is apes
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One person trimming photocopies in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns APES into SEPA, which I then cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown tint, like old photographs.

clue.text: Prison involved in raising of merit systems

indicators.note: raising of says the hidden letters are read backwards
involved in means the letters are wrapped up inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A jail concerned with lifting reward schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Prison involved' as the definition, but 'involved in' is the signal for letters inside 'merit systems'; 'raising of' reads them upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is British slang for jail, as in doing time in stir.

clue.text: Calls and records a sale

definitions.meaning: a shop till enters the amount of a purchase

explanation.surface: Phones and logs a transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both telephoning and keying a sale into a cash register.

clue.text: Wrong in law to accept soldiers suffering

indicators.note: to accept means taking in, so the soldiers go inside

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are soldiers, the other ranks

explanation.surface: An illegal act letting troops in causes misery.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: torment is severe distress, physical or mental.

clue.text: Crush fly

definitions.meaning: to crush hopes is to wreck them
to fly is to rush off quickly

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to smash or ruin, and to hurry away.

clue.text: Count Basie perhaps vetoed broadcast, needing editor's opinion

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out on air, so the word for vetoed is given by its sound

parts.note: vetoed means banned
a leader is a newspaper's editorial article giving its view

explanation.surface: A jazz great was kept off the airwaves, pending the editor's verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a noble title; Basie was a jazz musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Basie led a famous big band, an example of a jazz orchestra's head, hence perhaps.
